documents.title: Identification of dihydrokaempferol from Platycladus orientalis leaves as a potential therapeutic candidate for androgenetic alopecia through modulation of the KIT-mediated mast cell axis.
documents.abstract: Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) is the most common form of hair loss, characterized by progressive follicular miniaturization. Current therapies mainly target androgen signaling and show limited efficacy. Emerging evidence indicates that immune dysregulation contributes to AGA progression, but its therapeutic implications remain unclear. This study aimed to identify active compounds from Platycladus orientalis leaves and investigate their mechanisms in regulating AGA.

documents.title: Naturallyoccurring phytosterols in lipid nanoparticles induce rigidity reshape and endosome retention to enhance intracellular mRNA processing.
documents.abstract: Although lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have been widely used for mRNA delivery, understanding how cholesterol analogues modulate LNP properties and intracellular trafficking to enhance transfection efficiency remains essential for the rational design of next-generation delivery systems. This study investigated their structure-activity relationships and effects on mRNA delivery. We hypothesized that C-24 alkyl-substituted phytosterols enhance transfection by modulating LNP physicochemical properties and interactions with intracellular transport proteins. documents.title: Cryo-EM reveals a transmembrane allosteric site and activation mechanism for the SERCA calcium pump.
documents.abstract: Impaired sarco-endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase (SERCA) activity contributes to defective calcium handling and cellular dysfunction in cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, yet the structural basis of small-molecule SERCA activation has remained unknown. SERCA is a ubiquitous P-type ATPase that restores cytosolic Ca2+ to the sarco-endoplasmic reticulum and is essential for cardiac Ca2+ cycling and cellular energy homeostasis. Here, we used cryogenic electron microscopy to define how two chemically distinct activators, CDN1163 and UM-52, enhance SERCA function. Structures at 2.6 Å and 3.1 Å r

documents.title: [Engineering CaNAT for alkali tolerance to enable whole-cell catalysis of nonivamide synthesis via artificial intelligence].
documents.abstract: This study aims to improve the stability of N-acyltransferase (CaNAT), the key enzyme for nonivamide synthesis, under alkaline conditions, for enhancing nonivamide production as nonivamide exhibits higher solubility in alkaline environments and further decipher the stability improvement mechanism. First, the solubility of nonivamide in buffer solutions at different pH levels was determined. On the basis of the solubility results, the Acidophilic and Alkaliphilic Enzymes Predictive model (acidophilic and alkaliphilic enzymes predictive model, AAEPre) was first fine-tuned via MP-TRANS. documents.title: [Functional characterization of aldehyde:ferredoxin oxidoreductases in Clostridium ljungdahlii].
documents.abstract: To elucidate the functional division of aldehyde: ferredoxin oxidoreductase (AOR) isozymes in the ethanol synthesis of Clostridium ljungdahlii, we employed the CRISPR-Cas9 technology to construct single knockout mutants of aor1, aor2, and aor3 as well as the aor1/aor2 double knockout mutant. The functions of each AOR were systematically elucidated through fermentation experiments with CO as the sole carbon source, combined with quantitative real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) transcriptional analysis and protein structure prediction. documents.title: [Intelligent enzyme engineering paradigm evolution and future toolkits].
documents.abstract: Enzyme engineering is undergoing a profound paradigm shift from experience-driven approaches to a novel dual-driven framework integrating data and mechanism insights. Grounded in massive biological datasets, this paradigm deeply integrates computational biology, artificial intelligence (AI), and synthetic biology to establish an intelligent, end-to-end pipeline spanning discovery, design, and application. documents.title: [Catalytic bottlenecks and engineering strategies of post-modification enzymes heterologously expressed in microbial cells for plant natural product biosynthesis].
documents.abstract: Plant natural products represent a rich reservoir of pharmaceuticals and high-value bioproducts. However, their microbial biosynthesis is frequently constrained by inefficient post-modification steps. Key plant-derived post-modification enzymes, including cytochrome P450 monooxygenases, UDP-glycosyltransferases, O-methyltransferases, and prenyltransferases, often exhibit poor expression stability and low catalytic efficiency in heterologous microbial hosts. These limitations are primarily attributed to the absence of suitable membrane environments, protein misfolding, inefficient electron tran

documents.title: [Advances in the biomanufacturing of noncanonical amino acids].
documents.abstract: Noncanonical amino acids are essential molecular building blocks for expanding biochemical functionality and structural diversity, and have demonstrated broad application potential in areas such as innovative drug development, biomaterial construction and enzyme engineering. However, their conventional production has relied primarily on total chemical synthesis, which typically involves complex synthetic routes, limited stereoselectivity and serious environmental pollution, making it difficult to meet the demands of large-scale and sustainable manufacturing. documents.title: [Construction of a high-tolerance and high-yield nisin-producing Bacillus subtilis based on the evolution of tolerance elements].
documents.abstract: As a host that is generally recognized as safe (GRAS), Bacillus subtilis is considered an ideal chassis for the heterologous synthesis of the bacteriocin nisin. Nevertheless, nisin is a potent antimicrobial peptide, and its accumulation during heterologous synthesis exerts a strong inhibitory effect on the growth of the chassis, leading to "self-toxicity" and the stagnation of product synthesis. To address this issue, this study proposes a tolerance engineering strategy, overcoming this limitation through the rational design and modification of nisin transporters. documents.title: [Advances in ProteinMPNN-driven protein engineering].
documents.abstract: Biomanufacturing is a key pathway for promoting the green transformation of conventional production methods. Its core bottleneck lies in the difficulty of natural enzymes to meet the requirements of industrial applications, necessitating the customized modification of enzyme molecules through protein engineering. Conventional semi-rational design is limited by a narrow sequence search space, heavy reliance on known structural information, and high experimental screening costs, which make it difficult to achieve precise design of industrial-grade enzyme molecules. documents.title: Advances in photothermal nanozymes: from rational design to multifunctional theranostic platforms.
documents.abstract: Photothermal nanozymes integrate enzyme-like catalysis with photothermal conversion, where localized hyperthermia accelerates kinetics, improves substrate accessibility, and modulates biological barriers to achieve synergistic amplification beyond monotherapies. This review systematically surveys design strategies and applications, with highlights centered on three interconnected aspects. documents.title: Reprogramming IL‑2 Receptor-Binding Selectivity: A Computational Strategy for Engineering Receptor-Binding Profiles.
documents.abstract: Interleukin-2 (IL-2) immunotherapy is limited by off-target toxicity and the unintended activation of immunosuppressive regulatory T cells (Tregs). Here, we present a free-energy-guided computational and experimental workflow for stepwise reprogramming of the IL-2 receptor-binding profile. We first used molecular dynamics simulations, alanine scanning, interaction entropy-corrected binding free energy analysis, combinatorial mutation design, and thermodynamic integration to identify mutations that enhance IL-2Rα binding. documents.title: An Integrated Ligand- and Structure-Based Virtual Screening and Experimental Strategy for the Prediction of Chemically Diverse GLP-1R Agonists.
documents.abstract: The glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) plays a central role in metabolic regulation and is a major therapeutic target for obesity and diabetes. Peptide agonists, like semaglutide, targeting GLP-1R, remain among the most effective regulators of glucose metabolism and appetite. Nonetheless, recent reports of weight regain after treatment discontinuation sustain the interest in expanding the chemical diversity of GLP-1R ligands through drug discovery strategies. documents.title: Reinforcement Learning for Aligning Structure-Based Molecular Generation toward Make-on-Demand Chemical Spaces.
documents.abstract: Generative models for structure-based drug design have strong potential to accelerate early-stage drug discovery by enabling the conditional generation of target-specific molecules. However, a major bottleneck is that generated compounds are frequently difficult or impossible to synthesize, limiting their direct experimental validation and utility. We address this by optimizing for membership in make-on-demand chemical libraries, ensuring that generated molecules can be directly purchased and tested. To this end, we apply reinforcement learning to a pocket-conditioned generative molecular mode
documents.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling

documents.title: AARS1-Mediated GLUD1 K503 Lactylation Drives Colorectal Cancer Metastasis Through Post-Transcriptional Reprogramming.
documents.abstract: The prognosis of patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) largely depends on whether metastasis occurs. The Warburg effect leads to lactate accumulation and potential lysine lactylation (Kla), thereby promoting tumor initiation and progression. However, the role of non-histone Kla in CRC metastasis remains poorly understood. documents.title: Propolis, Quorum Sensing, and Biofilms in Canine Skin and Ear Infections: Evidence and Research Priorities.
documents.abstract: Background/Objectives: Secondary bacterial and yeast infections contribute to antimicrobial use in dogs with atopic dermatitis. This review examines whether propolis modulates quorum sensing (QS) or biofilm-associated traits relevant to canine skin and ear infections. Methods: The narrative synthesis was informed by a structured PubMed search on 12 October 2026, sensitivity searches, and targeted retrieval. documents.title: Antibacterial and Antifungal Activity of Anticancer-Active Diazaphenothiazine Derivatives: Experimental Evaluation and Molecular Docking Studies.
documents.abstract: Background/Objectives: The rapid emergence of antimicrobial resistance necessitates the development of new agents with enhanced efficacy and well-characterized mechanisms of action. This issue is particularly relevant to bacterial and fungal superinfections associated with anticancer therapy. This study evaluated the antibacterial and antifungal activities (expressed as IC50) of two diazaphenothiazine derivatives with previously demonstrated anticancer properties: the parent compound, 10H-2,7-diazaphenothiazine (BM1), and its 10-(1-methyl-4-nitroimidazole) derivative (BM2). documents.title: Predictive RNA-Ligand Binding Free Energy Perturbation through Preparatory Simulations and Polarizable Force Fields.
documents.abstract: Free energy perturbation (FEP) has become a cornerstone of structure-based drug design, yet its success has been built almost entirely on protein targets. Extending this physical rigor to RNA─an emerging and largely untapped therapeutic target class─confronts challenges that protein-ligand systems rarely impose: pronounced conformational flexibility, dense and highly anisotropic electrostatics, and ligand binding that frequently depends on direct metal coordination. documents.title: Enhancing Enzyme pH Adaptation for Industrial Biocatalysis: From Sequence-Dependent Engineering to Sequence-Independent Stabilization.
documents.abstract: Enzymes are indispensable biocatalysts in industrial processes, but their application is often restricted by narrow pH optima. Exposure to acidic or alkaline conditions alters the protonation states of ionizable residues, disrupts catalytic microenvironments and stabilizing interactions, and ultimately reduces activity, catalytic efficiency, or structural integrity. This limitation is particularly important in industrial sectors such as detergents, textiles, biorefineries, and therapeutic formulations, where operation under non-native pH conditions is frequently required. documents.title: Revealing the Mechanism of Porous Graphene in Styrene-Butadiene-Styrene/Crumb Rubber-Modified Asphalt: A Molecular Dynamics Study.
documents.abstract: Clarifying the interaction between graphene and styrene-butadiene-styrene block copolymer (SBS)/crumb rubber (CR)-modified asphalt is essential for applying graphene-modified asphalt. Therefore, the mechanical properties of SBS/CR-modified asphalt incorporating different dosages of porous graphene (PG) were investigated via molecular dynamics simulation to elucidate PG's role and mechanism in the SBS/CR/asphalt blend system. The results demonstrate that high-temperature elasticity and low-temperature flexibility of SBS/CR-modified asphalt were most effectively improved at a PG content of 2%. C

documents.title: Mechanistic Study of Xanthohumol Against Rheumatoid Arthritis via Regulation of p38/MAPK Pathway.
documents.abstract: To elucidate the molecular mechanism by which xanthohumol (XN) alleviates rheumatoid arthritis (RA), this study integrated network pharmacology prediction, proteomic screening, and molecular dynamics simulation to systematically evaluate the inhibitory effects and targets of XN in TNF-α-induced fibroblast-like synoviocytes (MH7A cells). XN dose-dependently reversed the pathological proliferation and invasive behavior of MH7A cells and down-regulated pro-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-1β and IL-6, as well as fibrosis/angiogenesis-related factors including TGF-β1 and VEGF. documents.title: Metalloenzymes as Biosynthetic Hooks for RiPP Natural Product Discovery: Genome Mining, Catalytic Innovation, and Biological Function.
documents.abstract: Ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs) constitute one of the most rapidly expanding classes of natural products, yet a substantial fraction of their biosynthetic diversity remains hidden within uncharacterized microbial genomes. Metal-dependent enzymes are increasingly emerging as powerful biosynthetic signatures because their cofactor requirements, sequence motifs, structural architectures, and genomic contexts can provide mechanistic clues to otherwise cryptic biochemical transformations. documents.title: Exploiting the Class IIa-Specific Hydrophobic Pocket: A Linker-Driven Strategy for Designing HDAC7-Targeted Inhibitors.
documents.abstract: Background/Objectives: Histone deacetylase 7 (HDAC7), a class IIa epigenetic regulator, is implicated in the progression of multiple malignancies; however, the development of selective HDAC7 inhibitors remains challenging due to the high structural conservation among HDAC isoforms, particularly with the closely related class IIb enzyme HDAC6. Methods: In this study, we screened a focused library of hydroxamate-based inhibitors to define the structural determinants governing HDAC7 isoform selectivity. documents.title: Integrating artificial intelligence prescreening with molecular dynamics for the design of peptide-based WWP1 inhibitors as promising therapeutic agents against breast cancer, including the triple-negative subtype.
documents.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is the most frequently diagnosed cancer and the second leading cause of cancer-related death in women. BC is classified into three primary subtypes, of which triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) carries the poorest prognosis because it lacks specific targetable markers. Preclinical studies of TNBC have consistently reported reduced tumor-suppressor activity of PTEN, activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. documents.title: Minimal Mutagenesis Resurrects Human Uricase with Attenuated Immunogenicity.
documents.abstract: The human uricase (UOX) gene was pseudogenized during evolution, leaving uric acid as the terminal product of purine metabolism. Heterologous uricases can elicit anti-drug antibodies, which limit their long-term use. Here, we restored activity to a human-pseudogene-derived uricase reference through molecular-evolution-guided rational design. Sequence alignment guided the construction of reversion mutants by overlap-extension PCR and two rounds of combinatorial optimization. documents.title: Computational and Experimental Studies of PSMA-Targeted Conjugates Designed for Subcellular Delivery of Theranostic Radiometals to Prostate Cancer Cells.
documents.abstract: Background: The membrane receptor prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a validated target for theranostic radioconjugates in the treatment and imaging of prostate cancer (PCa). Radioconjugates targeted at PSMA rely mostly on the peptidomimetic glutamate-urea-lysine (Glu-urea-Lys) binding motif to facilitate tumor accumulation. The combination of this binding motif with subcellular targeting moieties, such as acridine orange (AO) and triphenylphosphonium (TPP) derivatives, for nuclear and mitochondrial delivery, respectively, might open the way to innovative dual-target approaches. documents.title: Flexible Receptor Docking Provides Structural Models for the Recognition of 2‑Amino-heteroaryl-benzothiazole-6-anilide Derivatives by Lck via the CorrEA Method.
documents.abstract: Structural models of Lck bound to a chemically diverse series of 62 2-amino-heteroaryl-benzothiazole-6-anilide (AHBA) inhibitors were built to examine how the conformational state of the ATP-binding site shapes the structure-based interpretation of their potency. Docking to the static Lck crystal structure (PDB entry 1QPC) generated plausible complexes for only 54 of the 62 compounds, and produced essentially no relationship between docking scores and experimental pIC50 values, indicating that a single receptor conformation cannot capture how this scaffold is recognized. documents.title: Comparative Computational Investigation of Protonated Methamphetamine Inclusion Complexes with β-Cyclodextrin, 4-Sulfocalix[4]arene, and Cucurbit[7]uril.
documents.abstract: The molecular recognition of protonated methamphetamine (METH) enantiomers by β-cyclodextrin (β-CD), 4-sulfocalix[4]arene (SC[4]), and cucurbit[7]uril (CB[7]) was investigated using a comparative computational approach. Molecular docking was employed to identify favorable inclusion geometries, followed by density functional theory (DFT) calculations using the B97-D3/def2-SVP level of theory with the SMD water solvation model. documents.title: Combined DPD and MD Simulations of Surfactant-Coal-Water Interactions in Coal-Water Slurry.
documents.abstract: To understand the aggregate morphology and the interaction mechanism of the coal-water slurry (CWS) system, combined dissipative particle dynamics (DPD) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation investigation were used at 298 K. DPD simulations were used to examine aggregate morphology and component density profiles, while MD simulations were used to calculate radial distribution functions (RDFs). documents.title: Mining, Systematic Characterization, and Optimization of Key Elements for Marine-Derived GDP-L-Fucose Biosynthesis.
documents.abstract: GDP-L-fucose serves as a pivotal precursor for the synthesis of fucosylated human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs), exhibiting immense potential in infant nutrition, the development of anti-inflammatory pharmaceuticals, and clinical diagnostics. This study aimed to identify high-performance enzymatic components from marine sources to construct a green and efficient biosynthetic system. Based on thermodynamic analysis (ΔG'° ≈ -72.0 kJ/mol), seven core synthetic enzymes were identified from three marine bacterial strains. documents.title: Specifics of Classical Molecular Dynamics Simulation of the Raman Spectrum of the CO2 Fermi Dyad.
documents.abstract: Classical molecular dynamics is widely used to interpret the Raman and CARS spectra of supercritical CO2. However, the published positions of the Fermi dyad can differ by tens of cm-1. We show that the main cause of this scatter is the state preparation rather than the force field. documents.title: Tannic Acid Inhibits CaMKII-β Kinase Activity In Vitro and Displays Preclinical Anti-Tumor Activity in Ovarian Cancer Models.
documents.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) is characterized by delayed clinical diagnosis, intrinsic/acquired platinum chemoresistance, and a high postoperative recurrence rate, highlighting an unmet clinical need for new targeted therapeutic strategies. Herein, we integrated pan-cancer transcriptomic profiling, clinical tissue immunohistochemistry, siRNA-mediated gene silencing, co-immunoprecipitation, structure-based virtual ligand screening, in vitro kinase activity assays, cellular viability functional assays, and SK-OV-3 xenograft mouse models to preliminarily reveal that CaMKII-β may mediate OC progression and

documents.title: Lomerizine Suppresses JAK2/STAT3 Pathway Activation via CACNA1B in HNSCC.
documents.abstract: The JAK2/STAT3 pathway contributes to head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) progression. Using a STAT3 reporter assay, we screened a panel of 79 compounds and identified lomerizine, a calcium channel blocker approved in Japan for migraine prophylaxis, as an inhibitor of reporter activity. Lomerizine reduced JAK2 and STAT3 phosphorylation in CAL-27 cells and suppressed proliferation in the HNSCC cell models tested. documents.title: Molecular Dynamics Reveals Persistent Alternative Binding Conformations of a Donepezil-Melatonin Hybrid in Human Butyrylcholinesterase: Implications for Alzheimer's Disease Drug Discovery.
documents.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder in which declining acetylcholinesterase activity increases the relative importance of butyrylcholinesterase (BChE) in cholinergic regulation. Compound 4u, a donepezil-melatonin hybrid, was previously reported to inhibit human BChE with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration of 56 nM. documents.title: Secondary Metabolite Profiling, Anti-Mycobacterium tuberculosis Activity, Molecular Docking and Dynamics Studies of Carpobrotus edulis Leaf and Twig Extracts.
documents.abstract: Herein, we evaluated the antimycobacterial activity and cytotoxicity of Carpobrotus edulis (C. edulis) leaf and twig extracts, profiled their phytochemicals using LC-MS/MS, and investigated the predicted interactions of the putatively annotated metabolites towards the Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) InhA protein (PDB: 2NV6) using molecular docking. LC-MS/MS profiling and MS-DIAL spectral-library matching enabled the putative annotation of metabolites belonging to several chemical classes, including flavonoids, terpenoids, and nitrogen-containing compounds. documents.title: Cavity-Guided Chemiluminescent Probes for Drug-Metabolizing Enzymes: Rational Design , Activity Imaging, and Translational Applications.
documents.abstract: Drug-metabolizing enzymes (DMEs), which are crucial for xenobiotic biotransformation, profoundly influence therapeutic efficacy, drug safety, and physiological homeostasis. However, conventional analytical methods such as LC-MS/MS and fluorescence-based assays face limitations in background interference, spatiotemporal resolution, and in vivo imaging, while the structurally diverse catalytic cavities and overlapping substrate preferences of DMEs complicate isoform-specific activity assessment. documents.title: Identification and Fc-Formatting of Alpaca Single-Domain Antibodies Targeting the Nipah Virus Attachment Glycoprotein.
documents.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a WHO priority pathogen with case-fatality rates of 40-75%, and no antiviral therapeutic is licensed for human use. The attachment glycoprotein (G) mediates receptor engagement and is a validated target for neutralizing antibodies. Here, we aimed to isolate alpaca-derived single-domain antibodies (VHHs) against the NiV G head domain. documents.title: Machine-Learning-Guided Identification of Potent Osimertinib Analogues Targeting the EGFR Triple Mutant.
documents.abstract: Background: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations, including exon 19 deletions and L858R, are major drivers of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although osimertinib is an established EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), the emergence of T790M and C797S mutations can reduce its effectiveness. This study aimed to identify and computationally prioritize osimertinib analogues with potential activity against the EGFR L858R/T790M/C797S triple mutant using an integrated machine-learning-assisted cheminformatics and structure-based approach. documents.abstract: Background: Symphyotrichum novi-belgii (syn. Aster novi-belgii) belongs to the Asteraceae family and remains comparatively underexplored from a phytochemical and pharmacological perspective. Symphyotrichum novi-belgii remains poorly characterized in terms of organ-specific phytochemistry and anticancer relevance. Methods: In this study, methanolic extracts of the leaves, stems and roots of Symphyotrichum novi-belgii were characterized using FTIR and GC-MS. documents.title: Bioactive potential of Cynanchum acutum L. root extract revealed by phytochemical, biological, and molecular analyses.
documents.abstract: Cynanchum acutum L. is traditionally used as a medicinal plant, but its aqueous root extract, particularly from the Algerian Sahara, remains poorly investigated. This study integrated phytochemical profiling, in vitro antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and photoprotective assays, multivariate analysis, pharmacokinetic prediction, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to characterize its aqueous root extract and explore potential molecular contributors to the observed activities. documents.title: Scutellarin is associated with reduced Ischemia-related inflammation and changes in miR-124-5p, AKR1B1 and miR-155: a potential mechanistic model.
documents.abstract: This study investigated whether scutellarin can modulate inflammation-associated responses after cerebral ischemic injury in association with a potential miR-124-Akr1b1 regulatory relationship, together with parallel regulation of the pro-inflammatory miR-155.

documents.title: A reproducibility-audited, gate-based framework for early translational pharmacology: native-scale evidence, identifiability, and a 12-domain reporting checklist.
documents.abstract: Early translational pharmacology often combines docking scores, machine-learning structure predictions, and physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) simulations as if they formed a single evidentiary scale. This can create precise-looking but uncalibrated biological and clinical claims.

documents.title: Puerarin alleviates cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury-induced oxidative stress via the Neurl1/JAG1/Notch1 signaling pathway.
documents.abstract: Cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury (CIRI) remains a major challenge in stroke therapy, with limited effective neuroprotective interventions. Puerarin (Pue), a major bioactive isoflavone from Pueraria lobata, exhibits promising neuroprotective effects, yet its precise molecular targets and mechanisms remain unclear.

documents.title: Bisphenol a is associated with ovarian cancer chemoresistance via ecmCAF-mediated stromal remodeling: an integrative multi-omics study.
documents.abstract: BPA is a ubiquitous endocrine disruptor linked to ovarian cancer, yet its effect on chemotherapy efficacy is unknown. CAFs drive drug resistance via microenvironment remodeling. We investigated whether BPA exposure is associated with chemoresistance via CAF-mediated stromal reprogramming.

documents.title: Integrated Bioinformatics and Experimental Analyses Identify PSRC1 as a Prognostic Biomarker Associated with PI3K/AKT/mTOR Signaling in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
documents.abstract: To investigate the expression, prognostic significance, and biological functions of proline- and serine-rich coiled-coil 1 (PSRC1) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and to assess its association with WYE-125132 sensitivity.

documents.title: A hierarchical gating hypothesis for GABA-Mediated gut-liver communication: a mechanistic framework.
documents.abstract: γ  -Aminobutyric acid (GABA) can produce divergent outcomes in colitis and liver injury, but the conditions linking exposure to organ responses remain unresolved. We propose a hierarchical gating hypothesis in which compartment-specific GABA exposure is an upstream prerequisite. JAK3-associated immune status and CDK2-associated proliferative status are proposed as parallel effect modifiers, not a fixed linear signaling cascade. documents.title: Rational Design of Benzofuran-Linked Isatin Derivatives as MTDLs Targeting MAO-B and Cholinesterases: Synthesis, in silico Insights, and Neuroprotection Studies.
documents.abstract: Neurodegenerative disorders are multifactorial diseases associated with oxid active stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neurotransmitter imbalance, leading to progressive neuronal loss. Since monoamine oxidase-B (MAO-B) contributes to dopamine metabolism and reactive oxygen species generation, it represents an attractive therapeutic target for anti-neurodegenerative drug discovery.
